blocks.text: CHAPTER 1: INTRODUCTION
1.1 Background of the Project

Modern 24/7 commercial esports arenas and internet cafés depend on deterministic, standards-compliant physical and logical infrastructure to support high-frame-rate multiplayer gaming, real-time point-of-sale (POS) billing, local game-patch caching, quiet study pods, and uninterrupted wide-area connectivity. RJ Internet Café & Esports Inc. is establishing a three-branch Philippine network spanning Luzon (Clark Freeport Zone, Pampanga), Visayas (Cebu IT Park Flagship Headquarters), and Mindanao (Davao City), converging through a central Internet Service Provider (ISP) in Cebu City. Without a unified structured cabling architecture compliant with Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA, 2018) standards and Philippine Electrical Code (Institute of Integrated Electrical Engineers of the Philippines [IIEE], 2017) safety rules, commercial gaming venues frequently suffer from electromagnetic interference (EMI), packet loss, voltage sags, thermal throttling, and insecure flat-network topologies that expose billing servers to customer terminals.
1.2 Problem Statement
This proposal addresses five concrete engineering and operational infrastructure challenges:

How can three regional 1,040 sqm commercial floor plates be transformed from bare warm shells into zoned, life-safety-compliant 24/7 esports and internet café facilities with clear circulation and protected telecommunications rooms?

How can power distribution, air-conditioning feeders, and LED illumination be sized under PEC 2017 and European Committee for Standardization (CEN, 2021) benchmarks while maintaining physical EMI separation from data cabling?

How can a three-tier hierarchical structured cabling system guarantee ≤ 90 m Category 6 (Cat6) permanent links, complete drop-to-furniture-to-outlet parity, and zero spare-port shortfalls across all access switches?

How can a single dual-stack Variable Length Subnet Mask (VLSM) IPv4 and IPv6 addressing plan cleanly summarize all three regional sites while uniting Static, RIPv2/RIPng, EIGRP/EIGRPv6, redistribution, and bidirectional floating static failover at a single Cebu ISP hub?

How can strict inbound IPv4 and IPv6 Access Control Lists (ACLs) and Secure Shell (SSH) hardening isolate billing/POS servers, administrative LANs, and router management from customer gaming terminals without blocking legitimate HTTP/DNS services?
1.3 Project Objectives

General Objective: To design, cost, simulate, and verify a complete, standards-compliant multi-branch structured cabling and network infrastructure proposal for RJ Internet Café & Esports Inc. across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao converging at a central Cebu ISP.
Specific Objectives:
Develop conceptual Original (Before) and Modified (After) floor plans for three 1,040 sqm buildings in Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao meeting the minimum 1,000 sqm course requirement.

Produce five aligned CAD engineering plans—Floor, Electrical, Lighting, Structured Cabling, and Furniture & Fixtures—for the selected Cebu Flagship HQ site (ready for 1/8-board tracing-paper overlay defense).
Develop a transparent, formula-driven, Philippine-market (November 2026) consolidated budget excluding base building shell construction and benchmarked against the client target budget.
Calculate and validate an overlap-free dual-stack VLSM IPv4 (10.10.0.0/22) and IPv6 (2001:DB8:ACAD::/48) addressing plan with verified expansion headroom and stateful DHCPv4/DHCPv6 assignment.

Implement and harden multi-protocol routing (Static, RIPv2/RIPng, EIGRP/EIGRPv6, single-point redistribution on ISP-CEBU, passive LAN interfaces, bidirectional floating statics, SSH v2 on VTY 0–15, and four inbound IPv4/IPv6 security ACLs).

Deploy, verify, and document the inter-building network in Cisco Packet Tracer 9.0.1 alongside physical workspace backgrounds, bend-point cabling instructions, connectivity test matrices, and troubleshooting records.
1.4 Scope and Limitations

Scope: The proposal covers interior architectural fit-out, electrical distribution, LED lighting, structured cabling, active networking, IT workstations, furniture/HVAC costing, dual-stack addressing, routing, security hardening, and Cisco Packet Tracer 9.0.1 simulation for Building 2 (Cebu Flagship HQ, selected for all five detailed engineering plans) plus architectural before/after floor plates and multi-branch WAN integration for Building 1 (Clark) and Building 3 (Davao). All three sites utilize a 40.0 × 26.0 m (1,040.0 sqm) single-floor commercial plate; note that the ≥1,000 sqm single-floor configuration remains subject to final instructor confirmation if multi-story gross-area equivalence is later preferred.

Exclusions and Limitations: Base building structural shell construction, real-estate lease deposits, municipal building permits, and recurring staff payroll are excluded from the capital fit-out budget per course rules. Electrical and fire-protection layouts are academic engineering designs requiring review and sealing by a licensed Professional Electrical Engineer (PEE) prior to actual construction. Within Cisco Packet Tracer 9.0.1 (Cisco Systems, 2023b), physical-layer parameters such as Cat6 near-end crosstalk (NEXT), return loss, and optical OTDR attenuation cannot be measured directly and are therefore specified through field Fluke DSX-8000 certification in the BOQ. Logical routing, DHCP, redistribution, and ACL filtering were verified live on PT 9.0.1, while manual Physical Workspace device placement and bend-point screenshot capture are guided via a dedicated checklist for final defense assembly.
1.5 Description of the Proposed Organization

Organization Name: RJ Internet Café & Esports Inc.. Organization Type: Commercial 24/7 Internet Café, Esports Bootcamp Arena, Study/Work Pod Hub, Printing/Browsing Station, and Café Snack Pantry. Mission: To deliver tournament-grade, low-latency gaming, productive quiet-study spaces, and reliable digital printing services across major Philippine urban centers on a continuous 24/7 schedule. Departments and User Groups: (1) Standard & VIP Esports Gamers (30 active seats + 10-seat future gaming bay at HQ; 16 gaming seats per branch), (2) Study Pod & Quick-Browsing Customers (6 seats at HQ), (3) Cashier, POS & Printing Staff (2 POS bays, 2 network printers), (4) Management & IT Administration (4 HQ workstations including static SSH administrator IT-PC), and (5) Café Pantry & Operations Crew. For Cebu Flagship HQ fit-out budgeting (excluding building shell), the client target budget is set at ₱11,800,000.00 (~4.8% above the proposed grand total of ₱11,260,210.50, rounded to the nearest ₱100,000) as a realistic commercial capital cap.
1.6 Project Locations

The three regional facilities establish nationwide presence across the three primary Philippine island groups while leveraging Cebu City's central submarine fiber convergence for low-latency inter-branch WAN routing: Building 1 (Luzon) in Clark Freeport Zone, Angeles City, Pampanga (1,040 sqm conceptual Branch Café); Building 2 (Visayas — Selected Detailed Site) in Cebu IT Park, Apas, Cebu City (1,040 sqm conceptual Flagship HQ + central ISP convergence); and Building 3 (Mindanao) in Matina/Poblacion District, Davao City (1,040 sqm conceptual Branch Café). Full site parameters are tabulated in Chapter 3 (Table 3).
1.7 Significance of the Project

For end-users and esports competitors, the design guarantees sub-millisecond LAN switching, glare-controlled dimmable illumination, individual UPS brownout ride-through, and clean ergonomic workstations. For network administrators, hierarchical TIA-606-C labeling, centralized MDF/IDF enclosures, passive-interface hygiene, and strict inbound ACLs simplify troubleshooting and safeguard billing data. For management, an itemized, formula-driven budget staying 4.57% below target capital and pre-wired expansion bays protect long-term ROI.

blocks.text: CHAPTER 2: REVIEW OF RELATED LITERATURE
2.1 Structured Cabling Standards and Best Practices

Commercial premises telecommunications rely on modular subsystems defined by Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA, 2018) in ANSI/TIA-568.2-D and harmonized globally by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO, 2017) in ISO/IEC 11801-1:2017. Both standards restrict Category 6 (Cat6, 250 MHz) balanced twisted-pair horizontal permanent links to 90 m (100 m maximum channel including up to 10 m of work-area and patch cords) in a star topology from telecommunications rooms to work-area outlets. Effective lifecycle maintenance requires machine-printed identifiers across racks, patch panels, cables, and faceplates per ANSI/TIA-606-C (TIA, 2020), while grounding all racks and cable trays to a copper Telecommunications Main Grounding Busbar (TMGB) and Telecommunications Grounding Busbars (TGBs) per ANSI/TIA-607-D (TIA, 2019b) mitigates ground-potential differences and electrostatic discharge.
2.2 Building Floor Planning and Space Utilization

ANSI/TIA-569-E (TIA, 2019a) recommends centrally locating the Main Distribution Facility (MDF) away from wet walls and exterior thermal loads to shorten radial horizontal cable runs and avoid exceeding the 90 m copper limit. In Philippine commercial occupancies, Republic Act No. 9514—the Fire Code of the Philippines (Republic of the Philippines, 2008)—mandates unobstructed egress corridors, dual remote fire exits, illuminated exit signage, and fire-rated enclosure separation for electrical and server spaces. Acoustic zoning separating high-energy esports arenas from quiet study pods maximizes spatial utility across a 1,040 sqm single floor plate.
2.3 Electrical Wiring and Safety Considerations

The Philippine Electrical Code Part 1 (IIEE, 2017) establishes conductor ampacity, branch-circuit continuous loading limits (80% continuous utilization / 125% breaker sizing), receptacle demand factors (100% of first 10 kVA plus 50% of remainder), and motor/air-conditioning feeder sizing (100% of all units plus 25% of the largest single unit, applied once without double-counting). To prevent 60 Hz EMI from degrading gigabit Ethernet signals, ANSI/TIA-569-E (TIA, 2019a) specifies ≥ 300 mm parallel clearance between unshielded twisted-pair data trays and enclosed power conduits, with mandatory 90-degree crossings where intersections cannot be avoided.
2.4 Lighting Design and Illumination

EN 12464-1:2021 (CEN, 2021) defines maintained illuminance targets by visual task: 500 lux for cashier counters, administrative offices, study desks, and server rooms; 300 lux for general computer-display gaming and café dining areas; 200 lux for restrooms, lounges, and storage; and 150 lux for circulation corridors and stairwells. Simultaneously, ANSI/ASHRAE/IES Standard 90.1-2019 (American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers [ASHRAE], 2019) benchmarks commercial lighting power density (LPD) below 9.0 W/m², readily achieved using high-efficacy (105 lm/W) 40 W / 4,200 lm dimmable LED panels and restroom occupancy sensors.
2.5 Network Cabling, Devices, and Infrastructure

Enterprise campus networks adopt the Cisco three-tier hierarchical model—Core (MDF), Distribution (IDF), and Access—to isolate broadcast faults, simplify uplink aggregation, and guarantee predictable latency (Cisco Systems, 2023a; Odom, 2020). Multimode OM3 optical fiber links MDF core switches to regional IDFs with 10 Gbps headroom, while Layer-2 access switches (Cisco Catalyst 2960-24TT) dedicate all 24 FastEthernet ports to end-user drops and reserve GigabitEthernet uplinks (Gi0/1) for inter-tier trunks.
2.6 IP Addressing, VLSM, Routing, and Network Protocols

Classless VLSM conserves private RFC 1918 address space and enables contiguous per-site CIDR route summarization, minimizing upstream ISP routing table growth (Kurose & Ross, 2021; Odom, 2020). Heterogeneous WAN domains—Static routing, RIPv2/RIPng (hop-count metric, AD 120), and EIGRP/EIGRPv6 (composite bandwidth and delay metric, AD 90 internal / 170 external)—require a single redistribution boundary with explicit seed metrics to prevent routing loops (Odom, 2020). Passive LAN interfaces eliminate unnecessary multicast routing chatter on end-user segments, while floating static routes with administrative distances higher than the primary IGP provide deterministic backup failover. Standard VTY ACLs and inbound extended IPv4/IPv6 ACLs enforce least-privilege access at the ingress edge (Kurose & Ross, 2021).
2.7 Network Simulation and Testing Tools

Cisco Packet Tracer 9.0 (Cisco Systems, 2023b) supports dual-stack IOS 15.x routing, stateful DHCPv6, extended IPv4/IPv6 ACL inspection, Multiuser inter-instance peering, and scaled Physical Workspace layouts with Copper Patch Panels, Copper Wall Mounts, and cable-length attenuation checks. Geographic inter-branch visualization is anchored on public-domain 1:50m coastline datasets from Natural Earth (n.d.).
2.8 Synthesis and Application to the Proposed Project

Synthesizing the reviewed standards yields a unified engineering baseline for RJ Internet Café & Esports Inc.: a centrally positioned MDF keeps all 52 horizontal Cat6 runs ≤ 39.3 m (well inside the 90 m TIA-568.2-D limit), a 1.1 m corridor separation between power EMT and data wire-mesh trays exceeds TIA-569-E minimums, single-pass PEC 2017 demand calculations safely size a 200 A 3-phase MDP, 105 lm/W LED panels achieve 100% EN 12464-1 compliance at 6.76 W/m² LPD, and single-point Cebu ISP redistribution bridges RIPv2, EIGRP, and Static branches cleanly. blocks.text: 3.9 Structured Cabling Plan and Cost Analysis

The Structured Cabling Plan (Sheet C-1, Figure 6; Rack Elevation & 3-Tier Riser on Sheet C-2, Figure 7) implements a strict three-tier hierarchy with 52 horizontal Cat6 drops (42 PCs, 2 network printers, and 8 ceiling Wi-Fi 6 PoE APs) plus 2 in-rack server patches (SRV-1, SRV-2). Every workstation and AP drop follows the mandatory TIA-568.2-D physical path (PC/AP → Wall/Ceiling Keystone Jack → Cat6 Permanent Link → 24-Port Patch Panel → Access Switch → Distribution Switch → Core Switch → R-CEBU). blocks.text: 3.13 Routing and Protocol Design

Following the course protocol specification (OSPF excluded; EIGRP permitted), the multi-branch WAN employs three distinct routing domains united at ISP-CEBU as the single redistribution boundary: (1) Cebu Flagship HQ (R-CEBU) uses a static default route to ISP-CEBU paired with a standard static summary route on ISP-CEBU (10.10.0.0/24 and 2001:DB8:ACAD:1000::/52); (2) Clark Branch (R-CLARK) runs RIPv2 and RIPng (no auto-summary) on primary link WAN-CLARK-PRI with passive LAN/backup ports; (3) Davao Branch (R-DAVAO) runs EIGRP AS 100 and EIGRPv6 AS 100 (no auto-summary) on primary link WAN-DAVAO-PRI with passive LAN ports. ISP-CEBU performs two-way redistribution (static + connected + RIP ↔ EIGRP) using course seed metrics (RIP metric 2 + default-information originate; EIGRP metric 10000 100 255 1 1500). For resilience (third static route type), bidirectional IPv4 and IPv6 floating static routes run over dedicated backup serial links at AD 130 for Clark (> RIP AD 120) and AD 180 for Davao (> EIGRP external AD 170), including matching return floating static routes on ISP-CEBU to every branch LAN subnet.

Security Hardening & 4 Inbound ACL Objectives (IPv4 + IPv6 Mirror): Every router enforces encrypted secrets, MOTD banner, RSA 2048-bit SSH v2, console timeout, and full line vty 0 15 hardening (login local, transport input ssh, access-class 10 in, ipv6 access-class SSH-IT6 in). Four inbound ACL objectives protect the enterprise: (1) only static IT PCs (IT-PC 10.10.0.70, CLK-IT-PC 10.10.1.70, DVO-IT-PC 10.10.2.70 and IPv6 equivalents) may SSH any router; (2) only HQ-ADMIN-LAN may reach Billing/POS & Game-Cache server SRV-2 (10.10.0.99)—blocking HQ-GAMING-LAN (including customer Wi-Fi AP-01..AP-07), study pods, and both branches (note: staff Wi-Fi AP-08 resides on WPA2-authenticated HQ-ADMIN-LAN, clearly separated from customer Wi-Fi on HQ-GAMING-LAN); (3) Clark and Davao Gaming LANs cannot reach their local Admin/Staff LANs; and (4) Gaming LANs cannot FTP (TCP ports 21 and 20) to SRV-1 (10.10.0.98) while HTTP (TCP 80) and DNS (UDP/TCP 53) remain explicitly permitted.

Deploy a dedicated next-generation firewall (NGFW) with intrusion prevention (IPS) and dual-WAN SD-WAN failover at each site upon commercial rollout beyond the academic Cisco IOS 15.x baseline.
Implement 802.1X port authentication and WPA3-Enterprise RADIUS on Staff Wi-Fi (AP-08) plus captive-portal bandwidth shaping on Customer Wi-Fi (AP-01..AP-07).

The architecture is pre-engineered for seamless growth: the 96 sqm Future Gaming Bay already has overhead data tray stub-outs, two 20 A spare electrical circuits (PP-14), dedicated cooling (AC-03), and 10+ spare host addresses inside HQ-GAMING-LAN (10.10.0.0/26).
